blocks.text: NEW TESTAMENT
Bar-jesus. The sorcerer with the proconsul at Paphos who withstood Barnabas and Saul and was struck blind “for a season”.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“A certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew” (Acts 13:6)
ERA
New Testament AD 1–60
IN THE DAYS OF
Sergius Paulus
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW HE SPOKE
Acts calls him “a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew” and “Elymas the sorcerer”, but records no prophecy or word of his.
THE CALL
How he spoke
From the textActs calls him “a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew” and “Elymas the sorcerer”, but records no prophecy or word of his. Acts 13:6–8
Acts says he “withstood” Barnabas and Saul. Acts 13:8
BEFORE THE RULERS
Before Sergius Paulus
PROCONSUL OF CYPRUS
Sergius Paulus
“Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man;”
Acts 13:7 (KJV) →
PLACES
Where his story happened
Salamis · Where Barnabas and Saul landed on Cyprus
Paphos · Where they found Bar-jesus with the proconsul
Cyprus · “They sailed to Cyprus”
Seleucia · Where the journey to Cyprus began
SIGNS
Signs and wonders
WONDER
Struck blind “for a season”
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Paul (Saul)
Barnabas
Sergius Paulus
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textHe was struck blind “for a season”. Acts does not say whether his sight came back, or what became of him. Acts 13:11
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
It translates “sorcerer”
Albert Barnes; H. A. W. Meyer (English 1877–1879); M. R. Vincent (1887); R. J. Knowling (1900)

Barnes: “Elymas is the interpretation, not of the name Bar-jesus, but of the word rendered ‘the sorcerer.’” Vincent: “An Arabic word, meaning the wise, and equivalent to Magus.” Acts 13:8 [63][64][65][66]
It translates “Bar-jesus”
John Gill (1746–1748), after De Dieu and Hiller; J. A. Bengel (1742)
Gill holds that “Elymas” is the interpretation of “Bar-jesus”; Bengel says the two names “are in some way synonymous”. Acts 13:6–8 [67][68]
A different reading, Etoimas
F. Blass (as reported by Knowling, 1900)
Knowling reports manuscript support for the form “Etoimas”, which Blass reads and renders “Son of the Ready”. Acts 13:8 [66]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Acts 13
PASSAGES · 1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Acts records no word or prophecy of his own.
The page uses Acts’ own words for him: “a false prophet” (Acts 13:6).
Acts does not say whether he regained his sight.
